meta.keyed_by: Each indicator is keyed by its reading `type` from docs/schemas.md.
meta.source_rule: Every threshold-bearing field has a source: a URL, UNSOURCED (could not source yet) or DESIGN_CHOICE (our decision, recorded here).
meta.status_rule: status = worst of the amber/red checks below. See docs/knowledge_schema.md for exact semantics and data/score_reference.py for a tested reference implementation.
design_choices: Amber at bad-direction z >= 2 and red at z >= 3 (plan, 'Triage rules'). Where an indicator has a direction, only deviation in the bad direction counts. The plan wrote |z|; team to confirm.
z = (value - personal mean) / max(personal spread, min_spread). min_spread is a floor so 3 baseline runs cannot give a spread near zero (plan, fix 1).
An indicator can reach red without z (z: null) where a clinical limit or a streak is the right trigger.
Hazard tags use NASA HRP's five hazards. The mapping of each indicator to a hazard is our reading, not a NASA statement.
Baselines for non-lab types (sleep, mood, reaction time, lapses, sway) are built at run time from the astronaut's first runs. OSDR has no such data. Lab baselines come from data/baselines.json.

amber_limit.note: Amber when the night is under 7 h (AASM) or clearly below this person's usual.

red_limit.note: AASM/SRS: 6 or fewer hours is inadequate. Red needs 3 nights in a row (the 3 is our choice) so one bad night stays amber.

action.amber: Protect an 8 h sleep window tonight. Dim screens 1 h before, use eye mask and earplugs, no caffeine after midday.
action.red: Crew medical officer reviews workload. Move safety-critical tasks off the next shift and re-run STAND-REACT before them.

indicators.notes: Sleep need varies by person (AASM statement covers adults 18-60).

red_limit.note: A single-day score never makes red: mood is self-reported and noisy.

action.amber: Schedule private time and a call or message to family. Log one thing that went well today.
action.red: Private conversation with the crew medical officer. Book a behavioural health session with ground at the next link window.

indicators.notes: Compared with the stress classifier output (stress_label) to raise the mismatch flag. Check-in only: not a screening tool.

amber_limit.note: Personal baseline only. Our 20-60 s test is not a validated PVT.

action.amber: Take a 20 min rest or nap, hydrate, re-test before any critical task.
action.red: No safety-critical tasks until a re-test is back within baseline. Crew medical officer informed.

indicators.notes: Tune min_spread after 10 bench runs on the real station. Slow median and lapses come from one test, so the engine should not count both as separate amber indicators.

action.red: No safety-critical tasks until a re-test is back within baseline. Crew medical officer informed.

lapse_threshold_ms.note: 355 ms is the lapse threshold for the 3-min brief PVT (PVT-B); the standard 10-min PVT uses 500 ms. Our test is shorter than both, so lapses are indicative only. Part 3 owns the final value.

indicators.notes: Part 3 to confirm the threshold and push it to the firmware.

amber_limit.note: Personal baseline only. Not clinical posturography.

action.amber: Move slowly, keep a hand hold when changing posture, avoid rapid head turns for the next hour.
action.red: No EVA or vehicle operation. Crew medical officer checks balance and dizziness.

indicators.notes: Unit g is an assumption: confirm against the firmware (open question in docs/schemas.md). Tune min_spread after 10 bench runs. Part 3 to check the NTRS postural stability reference.

amber_limit.note: Lab-flagged (outside 65-99 mg/dL) or at least 2 SD from the person's own pre-flight baseline.

red_limit.note: Red is clinical only, not z: with 3 baseline draws a z score would make 103 mg/dL red. Below 54 is ADA level 2 hypoglycaemia. 250 is a placeholder, not yet sourced.

action.amber: Low: take 15 g fast carbohydrate and re-test in 15 min. High: hydrate, check the meal log, re-test fasting tomorrow and tell the crew medical officer.
action.red: Low: 15 g fast carbohydrate now, re-test in 15 min, crew medical officer present. High: crew medical officer reviews symptoms and fluids.

indicators.notes: ADA 15-15 rule covers the low-glucose steps only. The high-glucose steps are UNSOURCED. Needs a fasting reading. Baseline from NASA OSDR OSD-575 (data/baselines.json). Illustrates the method on 4 people and 3 pre-flight draws, not a medical finding.
